assert.//:
TWO urls as of P6.5 (#1814), with SEPARATE budgets — a single `assertions` block would have applied /login's 7000ms LCP to the public page, which is the number this phase exists to beat rather than to inherit. Measured 2026-10-15: this gate covered ONE of 395 live routes, and the one route P6.5 promises an LCP target for was not it.

/f/{handle} starts on `warn` DELIBERATELY. Its real LCP has never been measured, and the repo's rule for this file is that a budget is a REGRESSION GATE set just above a known-stable number, not an aspirational target asserted before anybody looked. The 2500ms in #1814's title is a goal; the `error` gate goes in once the three-run median is in a report. Asserting 2500 now would either pass by luck or fail a PR for a number nobody had measured.

assertMatrix.//: Re-baselined 2026-07-13. The /login page grew since the 2026-06-19 baseline (bundle + the ~6.3k-key i18n catalog shipped to unauthenticated pages): LCP is now a STABLE ~6.15s (3 runs 6.11-6.16s) and TBT is NOISY on shared CI runners (900-2630ms run-to-run). This stays a REGRESSION GATE, not an aspirational target — hard `error` budgets remain on the STABLE metrics (LCP 7000 = ~850ms headroom over 6.15s; CLS 0.25) so a real regression fails, while TBT is demoted to a non-failing `warn` (2500) because its run-to-run variance flaked the build by fractions of a ms (a median of 900.2 against a 900 budget). TBT is still tracked in the report. The June->July regression is real and worth a dedicated perf pass — the biggest lever is trimming the full message catalog sent to unauthenticated pages. simulate throttling is host-independent so CI matches local.

The public farm page. MEASURED 2026-10-15, FIVE runs with median aggregation — the first trustworthy figure for this page: LCP 3191 ms, FCP 1679 ms, Speed Index 1679 ms, TBT 286 ms, CLS 0.000, performance 87. This tree has the client chrome removed (#1874) and NOT the heading-font preload (#1877).

`aggregationMethod` is set PER ENTRY and that is not a style choice: at the top level lhci refuses with 'Cannot use assertMatrix with other options', which is how the first attempt at this fix failed. Without it the gate passed an LCP of 3672 ms against a 3200 ms error budget (#1878) — the default is not the per-metric median this file's reporter prints.

Five runs, not three. Two 3-run medians of the SAME commit came back 296 ms apart (3672 and 3376), so three samples cannot separate a change from the runner here. /login is documented below as stable to +/-25 ms over three; this page is not, and reading it as though it were produced two claims that had to be retracted — a 905 ms gain for #1874 and a 942 ms loss for #1877, neither supported.

3600 is the 5-run median plus ~13%, matching the headroom /login's gate uses over its own measurement. P6.5 wants 2500 ms and this is 691 ms short; the gate is a regression bound, not the target.
